# glinet_access_control (Resource)

Sets the access control mode of the router (`black_white_list`). The mode selects the MAC address list that the router uses: the block list (`glinet_client_block`) or the allow list (`glinet_client_allow`). The router has one access control configuration, so use one instance of this resource.

~> **Warning:** in allow-list mode, the router blocks each client that is not in the allow list, also the computer that runs Terraform. Read the description of `mode` before you set `allow_list`.

A mode change sends the new mode and the current list of that mode on the router, as the web UI does, so the entries of the list do not change. The provider sends the list as the router gives it. A change to allow-list mode fails when the allow list of the router is empty. When the mode on the router is the configured mode, the provider does not write. It is not known what a mode change does to the list of the other mode. The mode change is from the web UI code of firmware 4.8.3 and was not tested on a router. Destroy removes the resource from the Terraform state and does not change the router.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "glinet_access_control" "this" {
  mode = "block_list"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `mode` (String) Access control mode: `block_list` (`black` in the router API) blocks the clients in the block list; `allow_list` (`white`) blocks each client that is not in the allow list, also the computer that runs Terraform. Then Terraform and the web UI can lose the access to the router. Before you set `allow_list`, make sure that the allow list of the router has the MAC address of each client that must keep its access. `glinet_client_allow` writes only in allow-list mode, so add the first entries in the web UI. The web UI does not let a user save an allow list without the MAC address of the client that shows the web UI; the provider cannot do this check, and only refuses an empty allow list.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Always `access_control`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The import ID is always "access_control".
terraform import glinet_access_control.this access_control
```
